SONA 2016

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
This is going to be a the toughest State of the Nation address President Zuma has to deliver in his entire term of office. The nation and the world will be watching but can he save himself? There is a massive ground swell of no confidence across the country and the President impromptu walk about in Pretoria on Monday where he strongly denies there is anything amiss " everyone is happy it is just the media that is telling us we are unhappy" was a desperate last attempt to retain his common touch. But the storm clouds were brewing with the Constitution Court hearing the following day. A large a crowds of EFF and DA supporters marched to the Constitution Court in which some damning statements were made. Police Minister Nhkleko lawyer admitted that he was acting under instruction and Gauntlett acting on behalf of the President conceded that the Public Protector recommendations were to be upheld. "We do agree that the President must carry out the remedial action in the Public Protector's report … We accept that in this case the recommendations were administrative and unreviewed, and therefore binding.”.
Confidence in the President is at an all time low. The economy is reeling after Nenegate, his total lack of leadership during the racial debate in January, the crisis in education which the #Feesmustfall put on the agenda and COSATU are threatening a general strike in March.


Further information:
The laws that govern parliamentary process have been amended to ensure that the Presidents speech is not interrupted and we are told security measures have been beefed up yet Madame Speaker Mbete won't reveal the plan for fear of the EFF getting any advanced warning. Three marches are planned for Thursday-Seskona the housing movement who have become know as the Poo throwers, the DA and the Zuma must fall. The city hopes it will all be over by 5pm but ominously #Feesmustfall who initially applied to march have with drawn their application which could mean they will march in defiance of any application. Thursday 11th of February promises to be a reflection of the state of the nation and it appears the President wont be the only one having his say.

SONA 2016
With the economy in crisis, foreign investors losing confidence and the Nkandla controversy before the Constitutional Court, embattled President Jacob Zuma delivers his toughest state of the nation address yet. Carte Blanche’s John Webb reports from Parliament.


Script:


Script: The stage was set – South Africa was waiting to hear what the President had to say in his State of the Nation address. It came on the back of a turbulent week in politics and the press was out in full force.
Links “After Jacob Zuma’s apparent capitulation in the constitutional court earlier in the week speculation was rife about what sort of president we would see take to the podium for the state of the nation address would it be the combative Jacob Zuma that we saw in parliament last year or would his confidence have be severely dented
Script: The timing could not have been worse for Zuma – just three days earlier in the constitutional court his Advocate Jeremy Gaunlett contradicted two-years of denials on Nkandla, and undermined the many ANC members of Parliament who strenuously defended him.
Advocate Gauntlett.“We accept it is not just a recommendation she wanted certain things done and the undertaking is that those things should be done because they must be done
Script: Advocate Wim Trengove representing the EFF wasn’t having it
Trengove. What we have is president conduct in the breach of the constitution for almost 2 years and no explanation for it. If the president had come forward today and said I am sorry I had bad legal advice I acted in accordance with the legal advice I had all along and it was an error in good faith that would have been a different matter ”
Script: We asked Business Day’s editor Songezo Zibi what prompted the about turn
Songezo “What I think happened is that they realised that the court may reach an adverse finding in respect of his conduct in relation to the constitution and his oath of office and that might have very serious political consequences so it is much easier just to undertake to just pay back the money as was ordered by the public protector than face the other prospect.
Script: Constitutional expert Professor Pierre De Vos says ANC Members of parliament find themselves in an impossible position
Pierre “On the one hand they have to please the leadership of the party, whose going to have a decisive say in their retaining their job, on the other hand they have to comply with their constitutional duty to hold those very people in leadership accountable
Links Nkandlagate, Nenegate and his relationship and the Guptas all 3 have placed president Zuma under a significant amount of pressure but suggestions that his fate will be sealed by some MPs emboldened by a court victory might be over stating the case
Pierre The provision in the constitution that deals with the impeachment of the president is not a parentry provision it doesn’t require the National Assembly to impeach the presidents if it is found that there was a serious breach of the constitution and the law, it allows the national assembly to do so, so it is a discretion for the National Assembly, this means that the majority party in parliament they are the ones that can decide whether impeachment proceedings should go ahead and should actually be concluded and only they
Script. Vindicated after two years of slanderous attacks on The Public Protector and her office, Thuli Madonsela returned to Parliament in triumphant style
John: Was what happened in the Constitutional Court earlier this week one of your best days?
Thuli: I think so insofar as the powers of the office, yes it was quite an important day, not for me as a person, but for the institution, and of course for the rule of law and the principle of equality before the law
Script: But it’s been a volatile week and with threats of protest and counter protest and on the back of the #feesmustfall having successfully stormed the bastille-the state was taking no chances, security was at an all-time high says political analyst Judith February
Judith “Parliament being so cordoned off with barbed wire and razor wire that is something we have never seen and it does really give lie the sense of the notion of the peoples parliament and it seemed as though the people were nowhere near this event
Script: With threats of war from the ANC youth league, the streets of Cape Town were crawling with police. Three different protests took place across the city, all of them trying to get to parliament
Links ‘Well this is a security officer’s worst nightmare it exactly was anticipated two groups of protestors coming together
Upsound of Riot police at parliament
Script: And things turned nasty when EFF and ANC supporters slugged it out
Upsound of attack
Script: A disturbing sight which does not bode well for the upcoming Municipal elections
Judith “it is a metaphor for a president under siege and also a metaphor for a state that seems to be at odds, at war one might say, often with its citizens and it’s also part of a larger motif and that is the securitization of the state. We have seen it in various pieces of legislation during the Zuma years
Script: Emboldened by the Constitution Court hearing the EFF made a triumphant entrance disrupting the state of decorum in parliament. The speaker tried to get proceedings going reminding members of the joint sitting rules passed last November
Speaker Mbete ”No business other than the address by the president is entertained”
Julius Malema “Tell us the rules. Which rule? We must be governed by rules here we must be told which rule gives you such powers”
Speaker “Joint rule 14G
Julius Malema “You cannot just come and announce that this is what is going to happen this in a democratic parliament
John Steenhuizen “You have no right to unilaterally come to the house today and remove rules from the rule book “
Script: After much debate on the rules a compromise was reached but no sooner had the president begun more points of order were raised
Lekota “He broke his oath of office ”
Speaker” So you are free to leave the chamber
Ghadee “Four days we had 3 ministers un precidented reaction of the market that actually Nene cost the country 500 billion rand “
Script: This went on for an hour leaving those outside wondering if the President would ever get through his speech
Up sound “Zupta must fall Zupta must fall
Malema” Zuma is no longer a president that deserves a respect from anyone
Script: Finally the EFF withdrew holding what they called their own state of the nation address
Malema outside “This is a man who has said the ANC comes first and not South Africa”
Songezo “When somebody gives the president a really hard time you see a lot of people celebrating that, but I warn against getting used to that sort of thing because Parliament should project an image of institution that is serious that deals with issues, that reaches conclusions very quickly and holds the executives and other sectors of society to account.
Links “Behind those locked doors president Jacob Zuma continues his state of the nation address and for the time being a sense of normality has returned to the national assembly. “
Script: And for the first time President Zuma focused at length on the economy
Zuma” We have made an undertaking to spend public funds wisely and cut wasteful expenditure
Songezo “He had to deal with the economy but two things in the economy- State finances as well as a very clear strategy for growth he offered sort of a frame for both of them unfortunately I do not believe especially on state financers he went far enough
Judith “There is a conflation between the president and the weakness that we see, sometimes leads to a credibility gap because for example when the president talks about cost cutting and all the areas where we are going to have to be more austere and of course the question remains well what about Inkandla “
Zuma “We have heard the concerns raised about the performance of the state owned enterprises and companies. Many are of our SOE’s are performing well“
Songezo “The Government guarantees all or most of state owned enterprises debt. Eskom alone at junk status, by the way, owes more than 350 billion that is entirely guaranteed by the fiscas then you have got 21 billion in guarantees to SAA . We need to reduce the tax payers exposure to these guarantees and what he needed to say was that certain state owned enterprises will be partly or wholly privatised we need to disabuse ourselves to these ideological notions that this is bad because this is beginning to harm us. 2 Trillion in debt almost twice our national budget, it is unsustainable
Script: And with 3.6 million spent on this event what has changed?
Pierre “I think that people misunderstand the fact that what happens in the National Assembly in and of itself is not always that important and especially if it is like State of the Nation address. What happens in parliament is really important that it allows voters information about political parties and their behaviour to allow them to make up their minds who to vote for
Songezo “We are in trouble now- what we need is concrete action and very clear ideas and very clear direction that is what we need right now
Bongani “Will we get to those?
Songezo “I doubt it
Script: The theatre of politics played itself out - everybody got what they wanted – the President delivered his speech, and the opposition successfully voiced their disdain for Presidents Zuma’s leadership
Mmusi “South Africans are urgently looking for a plan, and I think the ANC, even tonight, are just walking out in a jubilant mood as though everything is fine, is an indicator of the distance they have from the people of South Africa
Script: This jubilation disguised what some say is a party divided and a leader under siege.
John: There have been suggestions in the press recently that Mr Zuma is losing power amongst the top echelons of the ANC, including the top six. Is this true?
Gwede: I don’t know where does that come from, people who say it will not be in the top six and they will speculate because they are not in the NEC. He is the president of the ANC, elected by Conference, and there is no other structure in the ANC that can reverse the decision of conference except another conference
Script: And with the country’s economy on the precipice risking a downgraded to junk status, everyone is looking forward to Finance Minister Pravin Gordon Budget speech to find some answers
